clue.text: Rather cool early Christian with authority

parts.note: St Luke, the gospel writer, was an early Christian
an arm of the law or state is its power, its authority

explanation.surface: A first-century believer who carries authority yet is somewhat aloof.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid or not quite cold is the sense: lukewarm water is rather cool, and so is a lukewarm reception.

clue.text: High-ranking officials to lead gunners onto ship

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for the metal lead
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Orders for artillerymen to board a vessel, with lead perhaps meaning to command them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' reads as a verb (to command) but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial idiom for the most senior people in an organisation, originally military officers with brass insignia.

clue.text: Problems associated with sudden withdrawal from remote country

parts.note: cold can mean distant or aloof, as a remote manner is
Turkey is a country straddling Europe and Asia

explanation.surface: Someone pulling out abruptly from a far-off land runs into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawal' suggests a retreat from the country; it is the drug-addict's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the unpleasant symptoms suffered when an addict stops a drug abruptly.

clue.text: Drew near artist, producer of pictures

parts.note: came means approached, drew near
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter who approached and turned out images.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drew' tempts as drawing a picture; with 'near' it means approached.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that takes photographs is literally something that produces pictures.

clue.text: Want chess player to sacrifice bishop

indicators.note: a chess player sacrificing a piece gives it up, so the bishop's letter is given up from the word

parts.note: Black is one of the two sides in a game of chess
B is the chess notation for a bishop

explanation.surface: A wish for a chess player to give up a bishop in a gambit.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, want means a shortage or absence of something, as in for want of money.

clue.text: Drag ladder leaving rehearsal

parts.note: a drag is a tiresome ordeal, a trial
a ladder in tights is a run

explanation.surface: A dragged-out ladder left behind after a practice session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag' and 'ladder' suggest hauling a ladder; they are an ordeal and a stocking flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice performance before the real thing is a test or a dry run.

clue.text: Comment on stain

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in letter headings
a mark is a stain or blemish

explanation.surface: Someone passing comment about a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun meaning an observation or brief statement, the same as a comment.

clue.text: It may affect the weather broadcast online

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the word online are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A forecast streamed over the internet influencing the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a weather bulletin going out online; it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific ocean-warming phenomenon is known for disrupting global weather patterns.

clue.text: A tailing copper cut back round roof

indicators.note: tailing means coming at the tail, so the A is placed at the very end

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: back tells us to read the synonym for cut from right to left

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A worker cutting copper sheet for a rounded roof, with an awkward trailing A.
explanation.definitionFit: A dome-shaped structure crowning a building is a small rounded roof.

clue.text: Squirrel, an hour after 12 noon, seen tucking into thick piece of bread, perhaps

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the time is placed within the bread

parts.note: a chunk is a thick piece, of bread for example
one o'clock in the afternoon is 1 PM, with the 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: A squirrel seen eating a hunk of bread at one in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 becomes the letter I, as crosswords often allow.
explanation.definitionFit: This striped North American rodent is a kind of ground squirrel.

clue.text: Sort of spin on holiday

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: A sort of spin, the PR kind, put on things while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg (or on) side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a delivery from a wrist-spinner turning from the leg side is a type of spin bowling.

clue.text: Wild cat devouring a rat's head and part of body

indicators.note: a cat devouring something takes it inside, so the other letters go within the cat's name

parts.note: the lynx is a wild cat

indicators.note: head points to the first letter of rat's

explanation.surface: A wild cat eating a rat's head and part of its body.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box in the throat is an organ, so a part of the body.

clue.text: Monk plugged in power tool and portable stove

indicators.note: plugged in means stuck inside, so the monk is placed within the tool

parts.note: a sander is an electric tool for smoothing surfaces
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

explanation.surface: A monk who plugged in a power tool and a camping stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugged in' reads as connecting to the mains; it means inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the lizard, the word names a small portable stove or heater used for warming or browning.

clue.text: Earthenware daughter left out

indicators.note: out means wrong or out of place, so the letters of left are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pottery left out for a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' reads as one phrase; 'out' is the anagram signal, turning LEFT into ELFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-and-white tin-glazed pottery made in the Dutch town of that name is a type of earthenware.

clue.text: Assorted 'semolina' clues, cryptic

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters of the two quoted words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A self-referential comment on mixed clues about a milk pudding being cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted and its synonym both mean of various kinds, mixed.

clue.text: Inspector, formerly a collier

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: An inspector who used to be a coal miner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who examines, such as an exam marker or official checker, is an inspector.

clue.text: Best in print, stylish

parts.note: a book that is out has been published, so is in print
smart means stylish or well-dressed

explanation.surface: The finest thing in print is a stylish one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective; it is the verb meaning to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to outdo or get the better of them by cleverness.

clue.text: Having to cut it by end of May shows harshness

parts.note: to sever is to cut

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of May

explanation.surface: Cutting things back by late May shows a harsh approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Severity is sternness or strictness, the quality of being harsh.

clue.text: Feel awkward about the old lady suggesting sex?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the mother
awkward suggests something clumsy and out of order, so the letters of feel are rearranged

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, MA

explanation.surface: Feeling uncomfortable about one's mother hinting at sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' scrambles FEEL into FE..LE, which goes about MA.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two sexes is the female; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Extremely clever to revise trust

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, first and last, of the word clever

parts.note: to edit is to revise a text

explanation.surface: Very clever to revise one's faith in someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to believe or trust it.

clue.text: Pretty area of land shown in musical from the east

indicators.note: shown in means displayed within, so the land goes inside the musical
in an across answer, reading from the east means right to left, so the musical's name is read backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Peron
a tract is an expanse of land

explanation.surface: A beautiful stretch of country featured in a stage musical set abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer east is the right-hand end, so 'from the east' means reading the musical's title right to left before the land is set inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasing to look at, good-looking: a synonym for pretty.

clue.text: In the end, book is printed on time

indicators.note: in a down answer, the book is printed on top of the time's letter, so it comes first

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

explanation.surface: Finally, the book goes to press on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning finally, after a long wait or delay.

clue.text: Foul play over Aintree champion?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for foul play is reversed

parts.note: foul play is a euphemism for murder

explanation.surface: Suspected cheating in a race at the Grand National course.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse of the Grand National; the famous horse won it three times, and the name famously spells a crime backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The racehorse is the most celebrated Grand National winner at Aintree, so a champion there.

clue.text: Graduate runs into French port, mostly for squid

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the graduate and runs enter the trimmed port
mostly means most but not all, so the port's last letter is dropped

parts.note: Calais is a French Channel port
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A graduate dashes into a French port, chiefly in search of squid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the port's final letter, and the graduate plus runs sit just before its last remaining letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word is used on menus for squid served as food, often fried in rings.

clue.text: The answer to this one must be written down

definitions.text: The answer to this one must be written down

parts.words: The answer to this one must be written down
parts.note: every ... answer is written in the grid, and this one runs down; the ... describes itself

explanation.surface: An instruction that the solution here has to be filled in, or set down vertically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' doubles as the direction of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This self-referential line is itself the thing in question: a crossword hint whose solution goes into the grid.

clue.text: Number of fundamental importance?

definitions.meaning: a counting number such as one, two, three, as opposed to an ordinal

explanation.surface: Asking whether some figure really matters a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: counting numbers are called by this name, and it also means principal or fundamental.

clue.text: Fairy godmother finally admitted to malice

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so the letter enters the word for malice

parts.note: spite is malice or ill will

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of godmother

explanation.surface: A fairy godmother who finally confessed to acting out of malice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted to' reads as confessing; it means let in.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf or small supernatural being of folklore is a fairy.

clue.text: Superior soldiers leading troops at the front in advance

indicators.note: leading means going ahead, so the soldiers come before the following letter

parts.note: better means superior
men are soldiers, the other ranks

indicators.note: at the front picks the first letter of troops

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers leading troops at the front line in an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advance' looks like a military push; it is improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvement or progress, an advance in one's condition.
